ledger.claim: The machine record is coherent as to identity, and the rider's initial burden is met on it: EV-TRIP-00713, EV-GPS-00713 and EV-FARE-00713 all carry trip_id TRP-00713, and the trace's first fix at 10:18:40 is the trip_record.started_at on the same artifact. Under POL-RD-08(a) the burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must answer with a specific artifact and a specific clause rather than with an assertion.

POL-RD-01 requires the threshold test to be run on gps_trace.trace_distance_km and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for it, and on the trace the figures are these: 6.83 km driven against an optimal route of 10.8 km, an excess of -3.97 km, or -36.76%. I do not assert a positive deviation, because the excess is negative and no POL-RD-02 refund arises; but those same figures are the rider's actual grievance, that the vehicle covered barely two thirds of the route the upfront fare was quoted for.

The driver's own in-app message is an admission against interest and needs no construction: the rider wrote 'This is a solo booking' at 10:25:20 (MSG-00713-001) and thirty seconds later the driver replied 'Then get out; I will end here' (MSG-00713-002), with the trip ending at 10:35:40. On the face of that artifact the rider did not leave of her own accord, and that is why the fare should not simply stand. The chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The driver's statement that 'she refused to share' presupposes a pooled itinerary on a booking the rider says was solo, and the only clause that could make a shared itinerary lawful here, POL-RD-12, runs off trip_record.vehicle_type: this record's vehicle_type is RYDE_X and not RYDE_POOL, and trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km is null. Nothing in the bundle identifies a co-rider, a matched itinerary or a second set of endpoints, so the explanation points to no artifact and carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

Any exoneration of the shortfall would have to run through POL-RD-03, which requires a traffic_advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, valid in a window covering the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, and matched by a route that leaves the corridor and rejoins it. The bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00713-01, is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and records that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. The absence is itself citable and it leaves POL-RD-03 unavailable on this record.

ledger.claim: I state the upfront arithmetic plainly, because the rider's case does not depend on disputing it: the fare_model on EV-FARE-00713 is UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd and total_charged are both 18.60, the ERP, airport-surcharge and waiting-time lines are all zero, and the POL-RD-11(a) remedy published on that artifact is therefore 0.00. That is precisely why the rider needs a ruling on whether the whole quote may be kept for a journey the vehicle did not complete, rather than a distance refund under POL-RD-02, which this fare model forecloses.

There is one more item the record does not reconcile, and it is a reason the file cannot be ruled on with confidence. EV-FARE-00713 carries per_km_rate_sgd 0.75 and distance_charged_km 6.8, yet its distance_fare line is 9.35, which is 12.47 km at the artifact's own stated per-kilometre rate, while the trace for the same trip measures 6.83 km. I do not allege a phantom gantry or a wrongly applied surcharge, and there are none on this bill; but a distance line that does not reconcile with either the billed distance or the trace at the artifact's own rate is a further reason a human should look at this file before the SGD 18.60 is kept.

POL-RD-01's default is NO_ACTION where no deviation is established, but that default governs the deviation question only. POL-RD-10 is expressed as mandatory - the Judge must NOT issue a final ruling and must instead escalate whenever any of its triggers holds - so a trigger under POL-RD-10 overrides the POL-RD-01 default rather than sitting behind it. The rider's route-deviation money claim being arithmetically empty is therefore not the end of the case.

The two accounts of why this ride ended cannot both be right and the machine record does not choose between them. The rider's account is carried by an admissible artifact at full weight - the chat log showing the driver ending the ride - and by a trace that stops 3.97 km short of the booked optimal route; the driver's account is carried by his statement and by the trip_record's COMPLETED status and the charged upfront fare. Mutually contradictory accounts of comparable strength is the situation POL-RD-10(7) names, and on this file the ruling cannot reach the 0.70 floor of POL-RD-10(1), because no artifact answers whether the booking was solo or why the vehicle stopped where it did. Escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal and replaces the monetary ruling, and under POL-GEN-03 it holds the disputed SGD 18.60 rather than leaving it collected - the outcome on this record that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement for the threshold test is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km. The trace records 6.83 km against a booked optimal route of 10.8 km, so the excess is negative (-3.97 km) — the vehicle travelled materially less than the optimal route, not more. Neither establishment test (excess greater than 20% of optimal, and greater than 0.8 km absolute) can be met, and POL-RD-01 provides that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The platform's own derived deviation block on the trace independently records status 'no deviation', with excess_km -3.97 and excess_pct -36.76 measured against the 10.8 km optimal. There is therefore no measured deviation on this trip for the rider's claim to attach to.

The gps_trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, the gaps array is empty, the maximum gap between consecutive fixes is 0.0 seconds against a 10 s sampling interval, and there are no straight-line jumps. This is a clean, complete trace, so the enhanced-corroboration regime in POL-RD-07(ii) and the escalation trigger in POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged, and the trace can be relied on directly.

The fare breakdown shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 18.60 and charged_total 18.60, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-11 governs: POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large any excess were claimed to be. The rider's only route-deviation remedies are (a) the excess of charged_total over the quoted fare plus properly chargeable pass-through lines, which is 0.00, and (b) a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09, which is also 0.00. The published pol_rd_11_remedy on the ledger is 0.00.

There are no pass-through or statutory lines on this trip to correct: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp and airport_surcharge are both 0.00, and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. No off-route gantry was charged, no surcharge was wrongly applied, and accordingly no standalone billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) and no pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 is available.

POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline applies only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL. This trip is recorded as RYDE_X, so the rider's narrative that the driver 'collected others' has no basis in the trip record, no co-rider itinerary exists, and the standard optimal route of 10.8 km governs — against which the trace lands 3.97 km short rather than over.

POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. She cannot discharge it: the trace is unimpaired (POL-RD-07 not engaged) and shows a negative excess, and no artifact in the bundle places the vehicle over the optimal route. An assertion of off-route carriage that cites no evidence of any excess carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

POL-RD-06's repeat-deviation check is not engaged at all, because POL-RD-01 records no deviation, let alone a MATERIAL one. For completeness, the citable counters are themselves clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so no pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 uplift or POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available on this record.

Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand. On this ledger payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00; on a rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION therefore leaves the agreed upfront fare in place, which is the correct outcome where no deviation is established and no pass-through correction is owed.

No party on this record asserts an external traffic cause — a queue, breakdown, closure or incident — for the route driven, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 are not engaged. The traffic_advisory is absent (EV-ADVIS-00713-01, status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) but, being uncited by either side as an exoneration, its absence is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and so it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5). It decides nothing.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: no refund is due and no escalation is warranted, and here is why.

This was an upfront-priced trip. EV-FARE-00713 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 18.60 and total_charged 18.60. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and there is no distance-or-time refund however the ride went. The rider's only remedies on such a trip are (a) the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-through lines, which is 18.60 - 18.60 = SGD 0.00, and (b) a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09. EV-FARE-00713 itemises no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty), no tolls, airport_surcharge 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00, so nothing is wrongly passed through and no billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) arises.

Nor is there a route deviation on which any distance refund could be founded. POL-RD-01 measures excess as actual less optimal distance and makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure. EV-GPS-00713 records 6.83 km against the booked optimal of 10.8 km (EV-TRIP-00713): excess -3.97 km, or -36.76%, with the platform's own derived block recording status 'no deviation'. Both establishment tests fail, so POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (coverage 100%, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s against a 10 s cadence), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged.

I have taken the rider's account seriously. EV-CHAT-00713 does confirm the ride ended early and that the driver wrote 'Then get out; I will end here', and the short trace is consistent with an early ending. But the trip record shows vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, with solo_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-12 has no application and the 'collected others' account finds no support in any artifact. The rider therefore cannot discharge the POL-RD-08 burden of showing an excess, and the driver's statement that she 'refused to share' is an assertion citing no evidence ID, carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and is in any event inconsistent with a solo product.

The rider asks for escalation and I decline it, because no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare ledger; the timestamps agree and none run backwards; the trace is unimpaired; no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a missing or deficient artifact. EV-ADVIS-00713-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, but neither side asserts a traffic cause, so its absence is an uncited gap, not a POL-RD-10(5) trigger, and (as POL-RD-13 provides) it decides nothing. The two accounts are not mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength under POL-RD-10(7): the driver's own message and his statement agree the ride ended early; only his unweighted statement differs on fault. The suggestion that the distance_fare line of 9.35 does not reconcile with the 0.75 per-km rate does not meet POL-RD-10(8): it is a distance charge whose counterpart is the trip's own distance (6.8 km on the trip record, 6.83 km on the trace), an upfront decomposition is not required to reproduce per_km x km, and EV-FARE-00713 carries no admissibility issue. POL-RD-06 is not engaged either: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips, so no pattern, uplift or conduct referral is available.

The finding rests on EV-GPS-00713, EV-TRIP-00713 and EV-FARE-00713, all at weight 1.0; confidence is 0.85, above the 0.70 floor. For the rider: the present state stands with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. If you believe the driver breached a solo booking or ended the trip without cause, that is a service-conduct matter this route-deviation policy does not monetise and this record does not prove. For the driver: the upfront fare stands and no compensation is awarded, as the billed distance (6.8 km) falls 0.03 km short of the trace (6.83 km), well under the 1.0 km POL-RD-04 threshold.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
